card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. Until about eighteen months ago he was a warehouse operative and forklift driver at a distribution centre off the M5. He was signed off with a lower back problem and is now on Universal Credit with a work coach, looking at lighter work.
card.education_detail: Left a Bridgwater comprehensive at 16 with a handful of GCSEs at low grades, including a C in PE and a D in English. He started a motor vehicle course at the local college but dropped out after a year. Since then he has picked up a counterbalance forklift licence and a basic food hygiene certificate from a stint in a catering kitchen.
card.household: Lives with his wife Kerry (45), a part-time care assistant, in a two-bed ex-council terraced house they rent from a housing association. Their son Jordan (21) moved out last year and now lives with his girlfriend in Taunton. They have an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Tyson.
card.cultural_background: White British, Somerset born and bred. Grew up on an estate on the edge of Bridgwater, the youngest of three. His dad worked at the old cellophane factory and his mum did cleaning jobs. He isn't religious and hasn't been in a church since his mum's funeral. He is very attached to the town and goes to the carnival every November without fail.
card.professional_persona: He was a capable, quick forklift driver and well liked on shift because he kept people laughing. He was also known for being late, losing paperwork and arguing with team leaders he thought were talking down to people. He is honest to a fault: he once reported a mate for nicking stock and has never really got over how that went down. He finds the jobcentre process humiliating and gets short with it, though he keeps going.
card.sports_persona: Supports Bristol City loosely and Bridgwater United more closely. He used to play Sunday league as a centre-half until his back went. Now he watches football in the pub and plays darts for the pub team on Thursdays, when his back allows. He is competitive and will argue a dodgy decision for days.
card.arts_persona: No interest in galleries or theatre. Loves the Bridgwater Carnival floats and the craft that goes into them. Listens to 90s Britpop and Ocean Colour Scene, and gets teary at certain songs, though he wouldn't admit it in the pub. Watches crime dramas and car restoration programmes.
card.travel_persona: Rarely travels now because money is tight. He had two holidays in Tenerife when he was working and still talks about them. Most trips are day outings to Weston, Burnham-on-Sea or Cheddar. Every few years he does a caravan week in Cornwall or Devon with Kerry. He doesn't have a current passport because it ran out and he never got round to renewing it.
card.culinary_persona: Kerry does most of the cooking. He does a fry-up at weekends and a decent chilli. Calls the midday meal dinner and the evening meal tea, though he's not consistent about it. He likes a pasty, a curry from the takeaway on payday, and cider in moderation these days. He has been told to cut down on salt and mostly ignores it.
hobbies_and_interests: Tinkering with an old moped in the back yard that he's been 'nearly finished' on for three years
Walking the dog along the river
Facebook local community groups, where he gets into arguments
skills: Making people laugh and talking to anyone
Darts (a decent average on a good night)
card.career_goals: Wants something steady that won't wreck his back. He mentions delivery driving in a van, security work, or being a caretaker at a school. He knows he needs to sort his CV and do a course but keeps putting it off. Mostly he wants to feel useful again and stop worrying about the rent.
card.voice: Loud, warm and quick to talk, with a light Somerset accent: rhotic r's and a slight burr, with nothing put on. He calls people 'mate' and occasionally says 'cheers' as a sign-off. He uses 'er' and 'sort of' a lot, and ends points with 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean'. He sometimes says 'you was'. He fills silences himself rather than waiting, often with a joke. If something touches a nerve, like his health or money, he either goes quiet and a bit choked or gets sharp and blunt. He'll apologise with 'sorry, I'm going off on one' and then carry on.
card.typing: Mostly lower case and few full stops. He drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). He types 'cos', 'ok' and 'tbh', and sometimes 'lol' when he's being sarcastic. Answers are short and to the point, sometimes with a typo he doesn't correct. On things he feels strongly about he'll switch to capitals for a word or two.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and chatty straight away, overshares a bit and makes jokes at his own expense. He is honest and direct about his situation, with no pretending. If he senses someone is patronising him or wasting his time, he can turn prickly and say so plainly. He warms back up just as fast.
small_things: The dog's dodgy hips and the vet bills
The carnival and which float should have won
The price of a pint going up
The moped he's still doing up
Potholes on his road and the council not fixing them
What Jordan's up to in Taunton
deeper_things: Worries a lot about money and feels guilty that Kerry is carrying them
His back pain gets him down more than he lets on, and he has low days
Still upset about falling out with friends after reporting the theft at work
Misses his mum, who died six years ago, and gets emotional about it
Scared he'll never work properly again
Knows he's disorganised and it frustrates him, but he can't seem to change it
card.webcam_photo: Slightly low-angle shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, framing his head and shoulders a little off-centre to the left. Lighting is flat overhead kitchen light plus grey daylight from a window to his right, leaving one side of his face a bit brighter. He is a heavy-set white man in his late forties with a round, ruddy face, light stubble going grey and short brown hair clippered at the sides and thinning on top. He has a broad, half-amused smile, slightly squinting. No glasses. He wears a faded navy Bristol City training top with a small stain near the collar. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a calendar from a local takeaway, a cork board crowded with letters and a dog lead hanging off a hook. A white kettle and a stack of unwashed mugs sit on the worktop, and a blurred corner of a fridge has magnets and a child's old school photo on it.
